lines: In 1700, England ruled growing American colonies and small trading outposts in India.
By 1783, King George III lost Thirteen Colonies in America, yet British rule expanded in India.
By 1815, defeating Napoleon at Waterloo left Britain commanding oceans and dominating global trade routes.
By 1914, King George V ruled a quarter of humanity, stretching from Cairo to Sydney.
By 1920, defeating the Ottoman Empire expanded British mandates across Iraq and Palestine to peak size.
By 1945, victory in World War Two bankrupted Britain, sparking Indian independence and rapid imperial collapse.
By 1960, Prime Minister Harold Macmillan oversaw rapid decolonization across Africa, dismantling the global empire.
The largest empire in history vanished in decades. Which former British colony prospered the most?
